I've been farming this land for twenty years. My mother and grandmother farmed before me. I don't read books about farming — I watch my neighbors, I remember what worked, I remember the bad years.

My land is 12 mu. Every mu does two crops: wheat in winter, maize in summer. That's what everyone in Quzhou does. That's what makes sense here.

**For wheat:** I'll plant in October like always. I buy improved seeds from the township supply shop — same kind I've used for the past several years. It does well. For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before plowing, then top-dress at jointing. My neighbor uses about the same amounts I do. I'll water four times — once before seeding to wet the bed, once in winter to protect roots from freezing, once at jointing, once at heading. I'll spray twice — once for weeds in spring, once for the rust and mildew that always comes. I use rotary tillage, always have. I expect around 450 jin per mu.

**For maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant maize. I always buy hybrid seed — everyone does, the yields are much better. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when it's knee-high. Summer rains usually help but if it's dry at silking I'll run the well pump. Two pesticide sprays — one for the army worm that's been bad some recent years. I'll rotary till lightly or skip deep tillage since the soil is still loose from wheat. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

My husband's brother works in the city and sends some money back, so we aren't desperate, but I still need the farm income. I won't try anything new this year — last year was decent, I'll repeat what worked.
